<div class="chapter-title-sanskrit">भगवद्गीता</div>

<div class="site-note">
<p>This English version was prepared from Google Translate output and revised using GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6 and Claude Opus 4.8/5.0, along with some manual editing. The aim was to produce an English translation that is readable, unbiased, and as literal as possible.</p>
<p>The Bhagavad Gita is part of the Mahabharata, Book 6, the Bhishma Parva, chapters 23–40. It is a dialogue set on a battlefield. Its protagonists are Arjuna, who hesitates to fight against his own relatives, and Krishna, an <i>avatar</i> of God. Its theme is <i>dharma</i>: action in accordance with one&#x27;s nature and the order of things. The answer is <i>yoga</i>: not gymnastics, but discipline (of action, knowledge, and love), free from attachment. The battle may perhaps be read as metaphorical. The text is rightly considered a synthesis and a masterpiece of Indian philosophy.</p>
</div>
